objective: Replace compose's in-form AttachmentPicker panel with a stats picker modal: the attach row's bar chart opens a second Dialog over the composer holding the stats navigator in select mode (Seasons and Players, down to a game's final score, a played box-score line or a career scope), with Cancel and a Select that stays disabled until a selectable row is chosen; and close the thread's carried risks R22 (a Dialog's initial focus), R23 (a failed lazy chunk stays failed), R25 (the picker's share of the navigator chunk), R29 (one ok() helper in api/), R30 (Back before a cold record's list lands) and R32 (cold-chunk findBy warm-ups).
acceptance_criteria: The bar chart (ChartColumnIcon, accessible name "Attach stats", at least 44 px square, a visible focus ring) opens the picker: UI-010's Dialog (components/ui/Dialog) titled "Attach stats", opened over the compose Dialog (one inside the other, as a ConfirmDialog opens inside the thread modal), with aria-haspopup="dialog" on the button and no aria-expanded or aria-controls. A reply address still offers no bar chart, and InlineComposer (the thread's reply box) still offers none. AttachmentPicker's panel, its three choice buttons and its native selects are gone; what is attached is still summarised under the attach row with "Remove attached stats", whether the picker has ever been opened or not, and a pre-filled /compose?link= address is still checked and attached on arrival with the same notes and the same words as today (prefilled-link.test.tsx passes unchanged but for the bar chart's new attributes, each change named in the PR).

The picker holds a SegmentedTabs bar Seasons / Players (the human, 2026-10-26: no Records tab, because a record is never attachable) over the shared StatsNavigator (components/stats-nav/) in its state-driven form: the stack is the picker's own state, no address changes while the picker is open, and every level control is a button (the adapter gives no levelHref). Seasons opens on the newest season, conference All, as on the Stats page; the picker starts afresh each time it opens (Seasons, the root level, nothing chosen).

Levels: Seasons → season (standings, the All / East / West bar, a team row opens the team level) → team (its record and its games, newest first; a game row opens that game's level instead of linking to /games/<id>) → game (the human, 2026-10-26: the game's level holds both game types): a "Final score" row first, then the box score's played lines (player, team, minutes, points, rebounds, assists), home side first, as playedLines orders them; and Players → the search (UI-010's SearchInput, at least 2 letters, debounced as today, the API's order, paged as on the Stats page's Players tab) → player (the player's name as the heading, then a Regular season row and a Playoffs row with games played and career points). StatsLevel grows by game, players and player kinds, every use narrows by kind, and the breadcrumb, Back and the focus rule are the navigator's (focus to the new level's heading when a control in the navigator opens or pops a level). On the Stats page nothing changes: a team's game row still links to /games/<id>, the Players tab still links to /players/<id>, and the records levels are untouched.

Selectable rows, and nothing else (the three data_link types, and the rules attachmentReads.ts applies today): a game's Final score when the game is completed (not both scores 0), a played line (seconds_played not null; a did-not-play line is not offered), and a career scope with games_played above 0. A row that is not selectable (an unplayed game's Final score, a scope with no games) is shown as plain text, never as a disabled control. A selectable row is a native radio input labelled with the row's words, in one radio group per level named by that level's heading, so a row is chosen by click, Space or the arrow keys; one choice is held across the whole picker (choosing another replaces it, and moving between levels keeps it), and one polite status line above the buttons names it ("Selected: <its summary>") or says "Nothing selected".

Cancel and Select: a footer under the navigator with Cancel (secondary) and Select (primary), Select disabled (the Button primitive's disabled state) until a selectable row is chosen. Select sends link-attached with that link to the mediator (which replaces any link already attached, as today), remembers its summary (describeGame / describeLine / describeCareer, so the summary under the attach row and Undo read as today), and closes the picker. Cancel, Escape and the backdrop close the picker and attach nothing. Escape in the picker closes only the picker, never the composer under it; however the picker closes, focus returns to the bar chart (the Dialog's own rule), and the draft's text, image and link are as they were.

R18: nothing inside the picker leaves it. Every game, team and player in the picker opens a level or is a radio, never a link to another page, so the picker never starts or continues a modal flow; a test pins that the picker renders no <a href> at all.

Reads (R29 and the brief's design note): the picker reads through src/api/ only, with the Stats page's query keys and staleTime (a team, a season or a game opened on Stats is not asked for again in the picker within its staleTime, and the other way round). The game detail and player detail reads it needs join src/api/stats.ts, typed from api/schema.d.ts; compose's attachmentReads.ts keeps only the address check, the selectability rules and the summary words, and reads nothing the picker reads; features/games/ and features/players/ keep their own reads unchanged. api/stats.ts and api/records.ts share one ok() helper in src/api/ instead of a private copy each.

Lazy and light (R25, R1): the picker is its own lazy chunk, fetched when the bar chart is first pressed (or warmed by the composer once it has rendered, whichever the Baseline settles), waited for inside the picker's Dialog behind a loading line, never the composer's or the page's Suspense; opening compose fetches no picker or navigator code. The records views (RecordsLevel, RecordLevel and their labels) are not in any chunk the picker loads, or the Baseline accepts their cost by name with its size; lazy-routes.test.ts and stats-nav-lazy.test.ts pin what the entry and the compose chunk may not import statically.

R23: a lazy chunk that fails to load is not cached as failed. When the composer's chunk (routes/ComposeModal.tsx's loadComposer) or the picker's chunk fails, the dialog shows an InlineAlert in place of its content ("We could not open this just now. Please try again.") with a Try again button; Try again, or closing and opening again, imports the chunk afresh, and a success then shows the content with no reload.

R22: a Dialog's initial focus is its Close button, set by Dialog itself after showModal() whatever the browser chose, unless a child moves it in its own effect (the reply box, a confirm's Cancel and the composer's text box keep doing so). In Chrome, closing compose that was opened from inside the detail modal puts focus on the detail's Close (FRONTEND-020 criterion 2, the browser row it missed), and opening the picker puts focus on the picker's Close.

R30: Back and the breadcrumb's first item on a record level always return to that record's own group, also when pressed on a cold /stats/records?record=<id> before its list lands (Back from a cold ?record=player-points-game lands on ?group=player with Player selected, at any moment); the records level's heading never names the wrong group meanwhile.

R32: every test file that reaches a lazy stats tab through the route table (StatsPage.test.tsx and routes/routes.test.tsx among them) warms its lazy chunks in a beforeAll, as d30f892 did for four files, so a first findBy never races a cold import under the full suite's load; no assertion changes.

Accessibility: the picker's tab bar is SegmentedTabs (tablist, arrow keys, one tab stop); every table keeps its caption, column scopes and row headers; every radio has a visible focus ring and a label naming the row; the status line is announced politely; at 360 wide nothing in the picker moves sideways but a table inside its ScrollTable; nothing prints null, undefined or NaN.

Every existing frontend test passes, except a test that pins AttachmentPicker's panel, its choice buttons and selects, the bar chart's aria-expanded, the Dialog's initial focus or the navigator's level union; such a test is changed or replaced in the test commit and named in the PR body (AttachmentPicker.test.tsx's criteria 1-5 and 12 move to the picker's tests; attach-row.test.tsx's disclosure checks; component-isolation.test.ts, which names AttachmentPicker.tsx), and any Director correction of a test is its own commit, before the implementation commit, named in the PR.

Baseline (provisional, the Director's draft, 2026-10-26; the skeptic's first pass declares it; before figures from origin/main 47b6ffd as bundle-budget.test.ts's own build measures them, gzip by zlib at the default level): (a) R19: no new dependency; frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-021.ts declares entryJsGzipGrowth at most 100 and entryJsRawGrowth at most 300 (only Dialog's focus line reaches the entry) and no entry CSS growth; changed: ComposePage at most 5,000 (before 5,373: the panel leaves), StatsNavigator at most 5,000 (before 4,696: the game and player levels; or less, if the records views split out); added: the picker's chunk at most 2,500 and its stylesheet at most 400; every other lazy output unchanged; if Rollup names the outputs otherwise the Director corrects the names in its own commit after a build of the implementation, keeping the sums (R20); no chunk 500,000 bytes raw or more, and the entry under 480,000 raw (R1); the before and after build tables are in the PR body; (b) lazy, as the criterion above, pinned by lazy-routes.test.ts and stats-nav-lazy.test.ts; (c) requests per screen, pinned with msw request counts in the test kit's staleTime-0 client through the real route table: opening compose makes 0 (1 for a pre-filled ?link=, as today); opening the picker cold makes at most 4 (the Seasons root, as a cold /stats/seasons), and 0 when Stats already read them within their staleTime; switching to Players makes 0, and a search makes 1 per settled query; opening a team makes 1, a game 1, a player 1; Back makes 0; choosing a row, Select and Cancel make 0; reopening the picker makes 0 within the staleTime; publishing with a link makes 1 POST /posts and the feed's refresh, as FRONTEND-020 pinned; (d) no freeze, recorded in the PR body (a host Playwright script, CPU throttled 4x over CDP, 360 wide, PerformanceObserver for longtask and layout-shift, a fresh browser context per cold run, five runs alternating origin/main and the branch, vite preview against the branch's backend on its own port reading the full load in fanwire_perf): with at least 40 cards on the feed, on opening the picker (chunk cold and warm), on switching Seasons and Players, on opening a team (its whole season of games), on opening a game (its box score), on Select and on Cancel, the median long task is at most 200 ms and no run over 250 ms (R4, R14); (e) cumulative layout shift under 0.1 in the worst of five runs, inside the picker while a level's read lands (each level holds its place with the shared Skeleton), and on the composer when the summary appears after Select; (f) every existing frontend test passes, but those the test commit changes and names; typecheck, lint and build pass.

0x08-frontend.md gets a section of its own for this unit: the picker modal, select mode and its levels, what is selectable, the reads in src/api/, the lazy chunk, and R22, R23, R25, R29, R30 and R32 as closed (FrontendUI/components.md rows go in a Director PR: no unit role may write FrontendUI/).

Browser rows (vite preview against the branch's backend on its own port, reading the full load in fanwire_perf; light and dark, 360 and 1280 wide, signed in): from the feed, open compose, press the bar chart, and attach in turn a game's final score, a played line and a career scope, each through the levels, each summary reading as today; Select is grey until a row is chosen; Cancel and Escape close only the picker; focus returns to the bar chart; Undo restores the previous link; a post with each link publishes; from inside the detail modal, compose's Close puts focus on the detail's Close (R22); with the network offline, opening the picker cold shows the failure and Try again recovers once it is back (R23); on a cold record address, Back pressed at once lands on that record's group (R30); keyboard only: the bar, every level control, the radios, Select and Cancel work with a visible ring; at 360 the picker's footer stays on screen and nothing moves sideways.
